correctness.rationale: For 2<=m<d the orthogonal split L=span(P_Le_d) ⊕ (L∩e_d^⊥) allows attainment of squared radius 1+min(h²,B/(1-B)); the transverse subspace is nonzero exactly because m>=2. Haar projection B has Beta(m/2,(d-m)/2) distribution, yielding the interior CDF and endpoint atom. Chi-square LLN/CLT and delta method yield the critical window variance 1/[2(1-rho)^2], while fixed k gives G_{d-k}/G_k and the claimed chi-square contact law. Independent distributional numeric checks for multiple d,m,h and high-dimensional regimes supplement but do not prove the analytic statements.
